- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 75–80 range), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture the “rebound” or “mean reversion” after peaks.
- Model underestimates the true decline in prices during the final 10–15 days of the 30-day window, particularly when prices are falling below 65.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, especially when historical mean is above 65 — should adjust downward by 2–5% relative to recent 7-day average.
- Model fails to account for “sudden drop” patterns near end of horizon — should apply a downward correction of 3–8% for days where true outcome drops below 55.
- Model overreacts to recent volatility — should dampen forecast sensitivity to short-term price swings (e.g., avoid 10%+ deviations from 7-day moving average).
